rows.label: -sS
rows.value: TCP SYN scan — professional default. Requires root.

rows.label: -sT
rows.value: TCP connect scan — no root needed, slower, more visible.

rows.label: --top-ports N
rows.value: Scan the N most common ports. Example: --top-ports 100

rows.label: -F
rows.value: Fast mode — top 100 ports only. Quick initial check.

rows.label: -T4
rows.value: Timing: fast (professional default for standard networks)

rows.label: -T2
rows.value: Timing: polite — slower, quieter, for sensitive networks

rows.label: --reason
rows.value: Show why Nmap assigned each port state (reset, syn-ack, no-response)

sections.heading: Scanning Commands — In Order of Use

rows.label: open
rows.value: SYN/ACK received. Service listening. Fingerprint and test.

rows.label: closed
rows.value: RST received from host. Port empty. Document and move on.

rows.label: filtered
rows.value: No response. Probe blocked. Unknown state. Investigate further.

rows.label: open|filtered
rows.value: UDP scan result — Nmap cannot distinguish open from filtered on UDP.

rows.label: 1. Confirm targets
rows.value: Only scan hosts confirmed alive in host discovery (Mission 1)

rows.label: 2. Default scan
rows.value: nmap -sS — quick initial picture of open, closed, filtered

rows.label: 4. Document separately
rows.value: Open, closed, and filtered — never grouped together

rows.label: 5. Flag filtered for follow-up
rows.value: Never mark filtered as safe or cleared
